business_definition: Number of census metropolitan areas the external market framework places in its strongest opportunity class under the balanced planning scenario.
formula: count of CMAs in the declared high-opportunity classification
grain: one row per CMA at the planning snapshot
filters: balanced scenario; CMAs with a full framework score
maturity_rule: not applicable; this is a current planning snapshot and is never applied retrospectively
null_handling: CMAs without a framework score are excluded from the count and reported separately as scale-only or no-evidence markets
interpretation: Where external SME market conditions look strongest. It is an external signal only and says nothing about the bank's share or presence.
limitation: External public aggregates only. Excludes bank market share, branch presence, competition, credit risk and acquisition cost.

business_definition: All synthetic leads captured in the declared operating period.
formula: count of leads
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: captured on or before the reporting cutoff
null_handling: leads with unresolved geography or industry are retained and grouped under explicit labels
interpretation: The size of the acquisition book being managed.
limitation: Synthetic volume calibrated by the generator; not a forecast of real demand.

business_definition: Leads that are still open and workable at the reporting cutoff.
formula: count of leads whose current status is not terminal
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: current status not in the terminal set
null_handling: none
interpretation: The live workload the team is carrying.
limitation: A point-in-time count; it does not show how long each lead has been open.

business_definition: Active leads whose recommended priority tier is P1 and which still need an operational step.
formula: count of actionable leads in tier P1
grain: one row per currently actionable lead
filters: actionable leads only; terminal leads excluded unless they need remediation
null_handling: leads with no priority decision cannot be P1 and are excluded
interpretation: The most urgent work in front of the team today.
limitation: Priority is a declared rule set awaiting business approval, not a validated predictor of value.

business_definition: Share of valid leads that reached an RM assignment.
formula: assigned leads divided by valid leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: valid leads only; invalid and merged leads excluded from the denominator
null_handling: a lead with no assignment timestamp counts as not assigned
interpretation: How reliably valid demand reaches an owner.
limitation: Does not distinguish a fast assignment from a slow one; see time to assignment.

business_definition: Share of assigned leads that reached a first two-way contact.
formula: contacted leads divided by assigned leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: assigned leads only
null_handling: a lead with no first-contact timestamp counts as not contacted
interpretation: Whether owned leads are actually being worked.
limitation: Contact is recorded from synthetic activity; it does not measure conversation quality.

business_definition: Share of contacted leads that reached qualified status.
formula: qualified leads divided by contacted leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: contacted leads only; cohort mature for qualification
maturity_rule: cohorts captured within 30 days of the cutoff are excluded from the denominator
null_handling: a lead with no qualification timestamp counts as not qualified
interpretation: How much contacted demand turns into real sales conversations.
limitation: Qualification is a synthetic status transition, not a credit or commercial decision.

business_definition: Share of mature valid leads that converted.
formula: converted leads divided by mature valid leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: valid leads captured at least 90 days before the cutoff
maturity_rule: cohorts captured within 90 days of the cutoff are excluded from both numerator and denominator so that recent leads are never counted as failed conversions
null_handling: a lead with no conversion timestamp counts as not converted
interpretation: The clearest available read on end-to-end acquisition effectiveness.
limitation: Entirely synthetic outcomes. Never evidence of real conversion behaviour and never used to tune any rule.

business_definition: Share of captured leads that were identified as duplicates.
formula: duplicate leads divided by captured leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: all captured leads
null_handling: a lead with no duplicate group counts as not a duplicate
interpretation: Intake data quality and wasted handling effort.
limitation: Duplicate detection is a synthetic rule set; real matching would differ.

business_definition: Share of first-contact SLA clocks that were met.
formula: SLA-eligible leads that did not breach divided by SLA-eligible leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: first-contact SLA clocks only (SLA-06 family)
maturity_rule: none; a clock that is still open and not yet past target is excluded from the denominator
null_handling: leads with no first-contact clock are excluded from both sides
interpretation: Whether the bank is meeting its own response promise.
limitation: Measured on synthetic clocks against a hypothetical SLA design.

business_definition: Number of first-contact SLA clocks that breached.
formula: count of breached first-contact clocks
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: first-contact SLA clocks only
null_handling: none
interpretation: The absolute volume of missed response promises.
limitation: A count, so it rises with volume; read it beside the compliance rate.

business_definition: Share of assigned leads that were moved to a different RM at least once.
formula: reassigned leads divided by assigned leads
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: assigned leads only
null_handling: none
interpretation: Churn in ownership, which costs discovery time and signals routing or capacity friction.
limitation: Does not separate a deliberate specialist hand-off from a capacity-driven move.

business_definition: Active leads that have no current owner or are sitting in a controlled queue.
formula: count of active leads with no owner or a queue code
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: active leads only
null_handling: none
interpretation: Demand that is captured but not yet in anyone's hands.
limitation: A queued lead may be correctly held (for example an unresolved duplicate) rather than neglected.

business_definition: Relationship managers whose latest observed utilization is at or above the declared warning level.
formula: count of RMs at or above the warning ratio
grain: RM x reporting month
filters: latest capacity snapshot at or before the cutoff
null_handling: RMs with no snapshot are reported separately as having no capacity evidence
interpretation: Who is close to being unable to take more work.
limitation: Capacity is a declared synthetic model (CAP-01 to CAP-10), not a measured workload.

business_definition: Share of routing decisions for which the capacity-aware policy produced an RM assignment.
formula: assigned routing decisions divided by all routing decisions
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: all decisions in the operational recommendation
null_handling: none
interpretation: Whether the declared rules can actually place the work.
limitation: A simulation over hypothetical rules; it is not a record of what happened.

business_definition: Operational recommendations whose simulated post-assignment utilization reached or passed the declared hard limit.
formula: count of recommendations at or above the hard limit
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: assigned recommendations only
null_handling: none
interpretation: Whether the capacity rule is being respected. The expected value is zero.
limitation: Measured against the capacity the historical policy produced; see the concentration caveat.

business_definition: Share of operational recommendations landing on the busiest tenth of relationship managers.
formula: recommendations to the busiest decile divided by all recommendations
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: assigned recommendations only; reindexed over every RM
null_handling: RMs receiving no recommendations are counted as zero rather than dropped
interpretation: How evenly the recommended work is spread. A high value is an operational risk.
limitation: Driven by the static capacity evidence; see the documented ledger limitation.

business_definition: Gini coefficient of operational recommendations across all relationship managers.
formula: standard Gini of the per-RM recommendation counts
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: assigned recommendations only; reindexed over every RM
null_handling: RMs receiving no recommendations are counted as zero
interpretation: Zero is perfectly even and one is fully concentrated.
limitation: A distributional measure only; it carries no information about whether the concentration is justified.

business_definition: Leads carrying a recorded data-quality problem that blocks or delays routing.
formula: count of leads with an unresolved geography, missing industry, pending validation or unresolved duplicate
grain: one row per reporting cutoff date
filters: all leads
null_handling: none
interpretation: The size of the intake-quality backlog.
limitation: Counts leads, not individual field defects; one lead may have several problems.

business_definition: Median hours from lead capture to first RM assignment.
formula: median of hours between capture and first assignment
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: assigned leads only
null_handling: unassigned leads are excluded rather than counted as an infinite delay
interpretation: How quickly demand reaches an owner.
limitation: A median hides the tail; read it with the SLA breach count.

business_definition: Median hours from first assignment to first two-way contact.
formula: median of hours between first assignment and first contact
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: contacted leads only
null_handling: leads never contacted are excluded rather than counted as an infinite delay
interpretation: How quickly owned leads are actually worked.
limitation: A median hides the tail; read it with the SLA breach count.

business_definition: Open leads not yet in a terminal status at the reporting cutoff.
formula: count of open leads
grain: one row per CMA at the planning snapshot
filters: active leads only
null_handling: none
interpretation: Where live demand is sitting geographically.
limitation: A stock measure; it does not show the rate of arrival or clearance.

business_definition: Open leads captured more than 30 days before the reporting cutoff.
formula: count of open leads older than the ageing threshold
grain: month x CMA x channel x segment x industry
filters: active leads only
null_handling: none
interpretation: Demand that has visibly stalled.
limitation: A lead may legitimately be in a long nurture cycle rather than neglected.

business_definition: Remaining workload points across relationship managers with a usable capacity snapshot.
formula: sum of capacity limit minus observed workload
grain: one row per CMA at the planning snapshot
filters: RMs with a capacity snapshot at or before the cutoff; attributed to their home territory CMA
null_handling: RMs with no usable snapshot contribute nothing and are counted in a separate no-evidence column
interpretation: Whether there is headroom to pursue more demand in a market.
limitation: Attributed by the RM home territory, so it understates coverage by RMs who also serve neighbouring territories.
